evidence: XVideo renders a self-closing video element and contains no unable-to-play-media fallback text. It already exposes a complete separate app-owned control group, loading status and actual error alert.

Chromium AccessibilityMediaElement::TextAlternative prioritizes IDS_MEDIA_PLAYBACK_ERROR over the ordinary accessible name when IsUnplayable is true; Restriction marks it disabled. IsUnplayable includes NETWORK_EMPTY and NETWORK_NO_SOURCE as well as element.error(). A lazy raw media node can therefore advertise an error while the app has not requested its source. The exact reason that the observed playing node retained that name is not established by static review.
ownedPlayerAccessibility.decision: Hide only the raw video rendering node from accessibility with aria-hidden=true; move its existing GIF/video name to a role=group on the app-owned player wrapper. Keep custom controls, loading status and the actual error/retry alert accessible. Do not add native controls, CSS hiding, inert, tabindex, source/intent changes, IPC or media-policy changes.
acceptance: Lazy normal-video and GIF players expose the correct named outer group while only the raw media node is aria-hidden; no native controls are added and no source is requested merely for accessibility.
Existing custom buttons and ranges remain outside aria-hidden ancestors; loading status remains exposed while awaiting a source.
A real source failure still exposes its role=alert and explicit retry control, with ordinary play disabled; the accessibility change must not hide or relabel a real failure as success.
Existing GIF loop, playback deadlines, single HLS start, pause/preview priority, cancellation and explicit-retry regressions remain green.

Parent separately checks actual UIA after hydration and playback: the misleading native disabled media node is absent, the named owned group and controls remain available, and real error reporting is retained. Unit DOM assertions alone are not actual UIA acceptance.
